chunks: O Allah, cause us to drink from Your rain
and do not make us among the despairing
and do not destroy us by years (of drought)
and do not punish us 'for what the foolish among us have committed'
O the Most Merciful of all!

key_terms.أَرْحَمَ الرَّاحِمِينَ: The Most Merciful of the merciful
key_terms.السُّفَهَاءُ: The foolish (those with limited understanding who commit sins)
key_terms.الْقَانِطِينَ: The despairing (those who lose hope in God's mercy)

ai.seo_question: What is the supplication for rain in Nahj al-Balagha asking for protection from?
ai.summary: This supplication, often cited from the sermons or letters of Imam Ali (AS) within the Nahj al-Balagha tradition, emphasizes the theological concept of 'Safah' (foolishness) as a distinct category of sin, allowing the righteous to be spared from the consequences of the general populace's errors. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on divine mercy overriding strict retribution, particularly in times of climatic distress, while invoking the attribute 'Arham al-Rahimin' to highlight Allah's comparative compassion. The prayer serves as a model for communal intercession, balancing hope for sustenance with humility regarding collective human frailty.
